title: “Perspectives on Healthy Aging – A Qualitative Survey as Part of an International Research Project” - Master's thesis as part of the international study “GPHA - Global Perspectives on Healthy Ageing”
summary:
Background of the project 
This project and our master's thesis deal with the fact that people worldwide are getting older. This creates new challenges for society, politics and the health system. The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared the years 2021 to 2030 the so-called UN decade of healthy aging. The aim is that people can live as independently, healthily and actively as possible, even at an older age. In our work, we conduct qualitative interviews with older people, political decision-makers in Germany and health care professionals. We want to investigate how healthy ageing is perceived and how the central fields of action defined by the WHO in relation to life in old age are understood and evaluated. 

Research objective 
The aim of our research is to investigate how older people, health care professionals and policy makers in Germany perceive and understand the central fields of action of the UN Decade of Healthy Aging. In addition, we analyze the extent to which the participation and participation of older people in Germany already exists from the point of view of experts and political decision-makers and how this can be further strengthened in order to achieve the goals of the UN Decade. In addition, we investigate what political requirements are seen and what effects are expected from the implementation of the goals of the UN decade of healthy aging in Germany. 

Methodology 
Our master's thesis is designed as a qualitative individual case study for Germany and is later to be embedded in a transnational case series within the framework of the GPHA-project. The selection of the participants takes place via a combination of direct address and recommendations within a limited examination room in the Frankfurt districts Innenstadt I–III as well as in Königstein. In total, the study area comprises a population of about 215,000 people.

interventions.name: Group 1: 5 older adults aged 65 and over are interviewed individually.
Group 2: Up to 3–6 healthcare professionals are interviewed in focus group discussions (or individually).
Group 3: Political decision-makers: Two political decision-makers are interviewed individually.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Older adults: 65+, living in the districts Innenstadt I-III in Frankfurt am Main or Königstein, capable of consenting.
• Health professionals: workers in the care of the elderly
• Political decision-makers: employees in relevant authorities or Organizations
• Sufficient knowledge of German for interviews or focus groups
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria:
• Not living or working in the regions mentioned
• Unable to give informed consent
• Organizational reasons to make participation impossible
